title: The Day Somebody Stole an Hour
skyStory: Overnight, the clocks sprang forward and an entire hour vanished into the sky. The first quarter moon, half lit in Gemini, is the prime suspect. It has two faces and an alibi for each one. Mercury, Gemini's ruler, is clearly in on it, whistling and juggling sixty stolen minutes behind its back. Somewhere a rooster is extremely confused. So is everyone.

reading: You are going to feel like you woke up in the wrong time zone. Lean into it. Today is a bit topsy-turvy anyway: daylight lingers longer, the evening feels stretched, and the moon is half lit and half plotting. It is also Pi Day, so circles are lucky.

Your mission is to find the missing hour. It is hiding somewhere in your day as a pocket of free time you did not expect, maybe twenty minutes, maybe forty. When you find it, do not fill it with work. Fill it with something round and joyful. A walk in a loop. A spin on a chair. A circle drawn freehand, perfectly, on the first try. Round things win today.
joel.mission: Draw the most perfect circle you can, freehand, in one go, and send a photo of it to Nancy as proof.
joel.omen: A clock still showing the old time somewhere. It means you have more time than you think today.
joel.elementWhy: Gemini moon blows the clocks around

reading: Gemini moons make everyone talk twice as much and listen half as well. You will be the exception. Today the Wood Rat listens to both sides of a conversation and spots the one sentence that solves everything. Say it quietly. Watch the room go oh.

Evening brings the first long, late daylight of the year. At around 6:30 pm, go to a window and notice: it is still bright. That light is your light, the light returning, the thing you were born on the solstice to promise. Stand in it for a moment, warm your pinky ruby in it, and know you kept your word to the world again this year.
nancy.mission: At 6:30 pm, find a window and stand in the late light for one full minute, ruby turned toward the sun.
nancy.omen: Sunlight on a wall long after it used to be dark. It means the light returning is returning just for you.

together.text: Pi Day plus the stolen hour. Each of you send the other a circle drawn freehand. The better circle wins the missing hour, which must then be spent on something gloriously unproductive. Mercury will judge, badly, and probably fudge the scores.
